rationale: The claim has two halves. (1) The personal-income-per-capita convergence regression (avg annual pcinc growth 1948-90 on log 1948 income) WAS reproduced in results/persistence_convergence.json: pcinc_convergence_slope=-0.01197 (paper -0.01; rounds to -0.01 at the paper's reported precision), pcinc_convergence_t=-7.13 i.e. |t|=7.13 (paper 6.8, ~4.9% off, within 5%), pcinc_convergence_r2=0.520 (paper 0.50, ~3.9% off, within 5%). This income half matches well. (2) The primary/named subject of the claim -- the manufacturing-wage convergence regression (slope -0.01, t=5.4, R^2=0.39) -- was NOT reproduced: mfg_wage_convergence_slope/_t/_r2 are all null, with mfg_wage_convergence_note stating 'Manufacturing production-worker AHE (1947-1990, SIC basis) is not reconstructable from free modern APIs' (confirmed in src/persistence_convergence.py lines 104-128, which set these to None and substitute the pcinc regression as the reconstructable analogue). Because half the claim's values (the income analogue) match within tolerance while the headline manufacturing-wage regression produced no value at all due to unavailable source data, the overall verdict is partial. fix_severity.json contained no entry bearing on this code path.
